summary: Dr. Naila Marir serves as an Assistant Professor in the Computer Science Department at Effat University. She earned her PhD in Computer Science and Technology from Harbin Engineering University, Harbin, China, and specializes in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. Her research is centered on Data-Centric AI, Federated Learning, and Big Data Analytics, with a strong emphasis on enhancing cybersecurity through Generative AI and Deep Learning. Dr. Marir's work advances Deep Learning techniques and their applications in Network Security, addressing critical challenges in data security and integrity. Additionally, she is dedicated to exploring Natural Language Processing and Sentiment Analysis to deepen understanding of human language for impactful real-world applications. Dr. Marir is committed to developing ethical AI solutions that prioritize privacy and security.

projects.title: A3L
projects.subtitle: Adaptive Adversarial Active Learning
projects.description: A multi-agent framework that integrates active adversarial sample selection with budget-constrained incremental retraining to enable label-efficient adversarial defense for cyber threat intelligence classification. A3L formalizes CTI robustness as a Markov Decision Process and introduces Adversarial Sample Utility — a novel acquisition function combining entropy and margin — to select only the most decision-boundary-proximal samples. The result: 92.5% robust accuracy using just 326 labeled samples, a 4.2× reduction over conventional adversarial training.

projects.title: HydroMind
projects.description: Autonomous hydroponic farming system powered by a 13-agent, 4-layer cognitive architecture running on Raspberry Pi and NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX. HydroMind combines reactive PID control, deliberative BDI planning, adaptive LSTM-based learning, and an LLM orchestrator (Llama 3) into a fully self-governing farm — from nutrient management and climate control to harvest planning and fault recovery. Features a Byzantine-resilient PBFT consensus protocol for strategic decisions and an on-device knowledge distillation pipeline that compresses cloud-trained models down to 85 KB for edge deployment. Aligned with Saudi Vision 2030 goals in food security and water conservation.

projects.title: Vision Beyond Sight
projects.description: Cloud-based mobile application that gives visually impaired users the ability to understand their surroundings through AI-powered scene description and speech synthesis. The user captures an image on their phone — the system sends it to a Vision AI model (GPT-4o Vision / Gemini), generates a natural language scene description, refines it with NLP, converts it to speech, and plays the audio back in under 3 seconds. Supports bilingual operation in Arabic and English, fully compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Evaluated with visually impaired participants using the SUS questionnaire.
projects.supervisors: Dr. Naila Marir · Dr. Passent Elkafrawy

projects.title: AEGIS
projects.description: LLM-powered penetration testing framework for multimodal AI security. AEGIS sits at the intersection of three research frontiers: adversarial machine learning, digital-twin-based red-teaming, and AI-adapted penetration testing. It uses large language models to autonomously generate adversarial attacks — evasion, poisoning, prompt injection, jailbreaking — against multimodal AI systems in a safe sandboxed environment, then evaluates model robustness and produces structured security reports. A senior capstone project that directly extends the A3L adversarial intelligence research line.
